# Approved differences between MORK's generated files before and after the migration to the layout of ADR-A126.
# One line for each triple only at the ref (only-at-ref) or only in the tree (only-in-tree).
# They fall into these groups, all for the maintainer to approve.
#   1. rdfs:comment replaces skos:definition as the definition of 230 terms and individuals of Mork.ttl.
#   2. 34 terms gain an rdfs:comment definition they lacked (31 in Mork.ttl, 3 in Executable.ttl).
#   3. 20 definitions and 13 scope notes become xsd:string typed literals, equal to plain literals in RDF 1.1,
#      because the grammar writes a text with a line break or markup as a typed literal.
#   4. Texts are reworded to drop a citation of a decision that is not published, a pointer to a document that does not exist,
#      and a semicolon. The rewording of sh:message in shapes/constraints.ttl changes its blank node, so three lines of that shape differ.
#   5. Both ontology headers gain a dct:description and a dct:creator, and Executable.ttl declares dct:creator
#      and dct:description as annotation properties.
ontology/mork/shapes/constraints.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMappingProductionGovernanceShape> <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#sparql> _:b3941cb22b1740180 .
ontology/mork/shapes/constraints.ttl only-at-ref _:b3941cb22b1740180 <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#message> "A GenerativeMapping in a ProductionMode mapping scheme must have progressed beyond Draft governance state (Reviewed, Active, or Superseded) and must declare a persistent identity before it compiles (ADR-A22). A Superseded mapping is historical, not unvetted, and is not rejected on that basis alone." .
ontology/mork/shapes/constraints.ttl only-at-ref _:b3941cb22b1740180 <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#select> """\n			PREFIX mork: <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#>\n			PREFIX fnd:  <https://www.nebularis.org/neuro-semantic/lattice/foundation#>\n			SELECT $this WHERE {\n				$this mork:mappingScheme ?scheme .\n				?scheme mork:compilationMode mork:ProductionMode .\n				FILTER (\n					NOT EXISTS { $this fnd:hasGovernanceState ?state . FILTER (?state != fnd:Draft) }\n					|| NOT EXISTS { $this fnd:hasIdentity ?identity }\n				)\n			}\n		""" .
ontology/mork/shapes/constraints.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMappingProductionGovernanceShape> <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#sparql> _:b2821637d6e9c07b8 .

A Superseded mapping is historical, not unvetted, and is not rejected on that basis alone." .

Deriving either from the absence of a fact, or deriving elg:Undetermined, would violate ADR-A24's positive-only restriction." .

ontology/mork/spec/Executable.ttl only-in-tree <https://www.nebularis.org/neuro-semantic/lattice/executable> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/creator> <https://github.com/nebularis> .
ontology/mork/spec/Executable.ttl only-in-tree <https://www.nebularis.org/neuro-semantic/lattice/executable> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/description> """MORK states a mapping between a source and a target ontology as data. A mapping is a node in a graph that says which source element corresponds to which target element, in which stratum of the target (its classes, its properties or its individuals), how closely, how confidently and under what governance. Mappings compose into a directed acyclic graph, so that the order in which they must run is derived and never written down.\n\nA compiler reads the mapping graph and writes executable artefacts, such as RML mappings, SPARQL queries, SHACL shapes and SWRL rules. A language model may propose the graph, and a validator and a person then check it before anything compiles. The module also holds Executable, the vocabulary for the plans, artefacts and diagnostics that MORK's Eligibility backends produce.""" .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The class of all DataMapping individuals whose evaluation produces a constraint, inference, transformation, or projection artefact (SHACL shape, SWRL rule, RML triples map, projection mapping records, or future artefact types). Serves as the common superclass for ShapeMapping, RuleMapping, TransformMapping, and ProjectionMapping, and as the domain for shared properties (hasParameterBinding, hasTargetingSpec, dependsOnMapping)." .
ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> "GenerativeMapping is not an equivalence class — it has no structural characterisation that would allow automatic classification. Membership is inferred via subclass relationships from ShapeMapping, RuleMapping, TransformMapping, or ProjectionMapping. Foundation alignment (ADR-A22): subclassing fnd:Governable and fnd:Versioned requires exactly one fnd:hasGovernanceState and one fnd:hasIdentity per instance at the OWL level, matching the pattern srf:SurfaceContract already uses. This is additive to, not a replacement for, the pre-existing reviewStatus (on *Provenance individuals), supersedes, mappingVersion, and deprecationReason properties, which remain valid and are unchanged; see ontology/mork/docs/governance-and-versioning-migration.md for how the two relate and for the backward-compatibility story. Production-mode compilation gating on governance state is a SHACL-level, mode-conditional check (mork:GenerativeMappingProductionGovernanceShape: beyond Draft, plus identity), not an unconditional OWL requirement — a draft-mode mapping with no governance state asserted yet is incomplete, not inconsistent." .

IntentNode individuals form a bounded join-semilattice under :refinesIntent.\n\nSubtypes capture the principal categories of insurance product and eligibility criteria: QualitativeIntent, QuantitativeConstraint, SpatialScope, TemporalScope, ExclusionIntent, InclusionIntent. These subtypes are not mutually disjoint.""" .

It carries jurisdiction, effective period, and provenance metadata.\n\nThe IntentScheme occupies a position between natural language and ontological commitment. It captures what the user means without committing to how that meaning is realised in a target ontology.""" .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#TransformMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> """A generative mapping that, when compiled, produces an RML/R2RML triples map as a first-class RDF graph object (an rr:TriplesMap individual with structured subject map, predicate-object maps, and logical source).\n\nClassification as TransformMapping is inferred from the presence of the generatesTransformDefinition property pointing to an rr:TriplesMap individual, following the same definitional pattern as ShapeMapping (≡ DataMapping ⊓ ∃generatesShapeDefinition.sh:Shape) and RuleMapping (≡ DataMapping ⊓ ∃generatesRuleDefinition.swrl:Imp).\n\nThe generated triples map is structured RDF — not a serialised mapping file. ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#TransformMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """Unlike ShapeMapping and RuleMapping, an ordinary (non-generative) DataMapping is already RML-compilable in the ingress direction — a compiler may walk any Datum, Lookup, or R-Box assertion node and emit a triples map without that node ever being asserted as a TransformMapping. TransformMapping exists to make that compiled artefact a first-class, queryable, provenance-bearing graph object exactly where a deployment needs to trace "which mapping produced this triples map" — the same governance guarantee ShapeMapping and RuleMapping already give SHACL shapes and SWRL rules.\n\nTransformMapping is also the natural target for the reverse (egress) direction: a DataMapping whose source is itself part of the ontology (e.g. a qnt:Quantity or qnt:Range chain) and whose rr:TriplesMap projects that chain out to a flatter, deployment-specific representation. egressProjection (§ DataMapping) names the target Representation; generatesTransformDefinition names the compiled artefact that performs the projection.""" .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#broaderApplicative> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> """Models contextual (Kleisli) composition for the context monad. This causes any compositeNarrowerMapping to be applied within the context (i.e., mapping outcome) of the object, rather than the subject.\n\nUsed when a mapping needs to interact with the outcome of a prior mapping, for example a compositeBroader or hypothesisMapping. Please read the skos:scopeNote for the expected behaviours.""" .
ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#broaderApplicative> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """All compositeNarrowerMappings will be applied to the context (i.e., the axioms resulting as the *outcome* of the broaderApplicative object mapping). This implies the following rules:\n\n- The broaderApplicative object must be a DataMapping or subclass thereof.\n- An exactRBoxMatch or inverseRBoxMatch MUST be provided to indicate the relationship between the subject (outcome of this mapping) and the object (on the other end of the relationship).\n\nSpecifically, this instruction means:\n\n- Consider the context/outcome axiom of this (subject) mapping, refer to it as the "child"\n- Look up the broaderApplicative mapping, refer to it as the "parent"\n- Find the axiom (or entry point into a digraph of axioms) created by the "parent" mapping, that is related to the "child" axiom along the relationship defined by the exactRBoxMatch\n- Apply the compositeNarrowerMappings of the subject (mapping) to the parent's axiom(s) and not to the child's\n\nFormally, this is modelled as Kleisli composition for a context monad (see Foundations §2.4). The co-occurrence constraint requiring an exactRBoxMatch is enforced by GCI Axiom 2.14a.""" .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-at-ref <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#precedes> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """The precedence relation is the transitive closure of structural dependency relationships. \nIt is derived from: compositeBroaderMapping (inverse), broaderApplicative (inverse), dependentMapping (inverse), and templateMapping (inverse) via subproperty axioms, plus conditional rules (SWRL) for T-Box before A-Box, identity resolution, and template child correlation.\n\nA transitive property cannot also be asymmetric or irreflexive in OWL 2 DL, and neither characteristic would catch a cycle of three or more mappings. mork:PrecedenceAcyclicityShape (shapes/constraints.ttl) rejects every cycle instead, through this property and the properties it is derived from (ADR-A97).""" .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> "The class of all DataMapping individuals whose evaluation produces a constraint, inference, transformation, or projection artefact (SHACL shape, SWRL rule, RML triples map, projection mapping records, or future artefact types). ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#GenerativeMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> "GenerativeMapping is not an equivalence class — it has no structural characterisation that would allow automatic classification. Membership is inferred via subclass relationships from ShapeMapping, RuleMapping, TransformMapping, or ProjectionMapping. Foundation alignment: subclassing fnd:Governable and fnd:Versioned requires exactly one fnd:hasGovernanceState and one fnd:hasIdentity per instance at the OWL level, matching the pattern srf:SurfaceContract already uses. This is additive to, not a replacement for, the pre-existing reviewStatus (on *Provenance individuals), supersedes, mappingVersion, and deprecationReason properties, which remain valid and are unchanged. Production-mode compilation gating on governance state is a SHACL-level, mode-conditional check (mork:GenerativeMappingProductionGovernanceShape: beyond Draft, plus identity), not an unconditional OWL requirement — a draft-mode mapping with no governance state asserted yet is incomplete, not inconsistent." .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#TransformMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> """A generative mapping that, when compiled, produces an RML/R2RML triples map as a first-class RDF graph object (an rr:TriplesMap individual with structured subject map, predicate-object maps, and logical source).\n\nClassification as TransformMapping is inferred from the presence of the generatesTransformDefinition property pointing to an rr:TriplesMap individual, following the same definitional pattern as ShapeMapping (≡ DataMapping ⊓ ∃generatesShapeDefinition.sh:Shape) and RuleMapping (≡ DataMapping ⊓ ∃generatesRuleDefinition.swrl:Imp).\n\nThe generated triples map is structured RDF — not a serialised mapping file. ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#TransformMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """Unlike ShapeMapping and RuleMapping, an ordinary (non-generative) DataMapping is already RML-compilable in the ingress direction — a compiler may walk any Datum, Lookup, or R-Box assertion node and emit a triples map without that node ever being asserted as a TransformMapping. TransformMapping exists to make that compiled artefact a first-class, queryable, provenance-bearing graph object exactly where a deployment needs to trace "which mapping produced this triples map" — the same governance guarantee ShapeMapping and RuleMapping already give SHACL shapes and SWRL rules.\n\nTransformMapping is also the natural target for the reverse (egress) direction: a DataMapping whose source is itself part of the ontology (e.g. a qnt:Quantity or qnt:Range chain) and whose rr:TriplesMap projects that chain out to a flatter, deployment-specific representation. egressProjection (§ DataMapping) names the target Representation. generatesTransformDefinition names the compiled artefact that performs the projection."""^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string> .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#broaderApplicative> <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment> """Models contextual (Kleisli) composition for the context monad. This causes any compositeNarrowerMapping to be applied within the context (i.e., mapping outcome) of the object, rather than the subject.\n\nUsed when a mapping needs to interact with the outcome of a prior mapping, for example a compositeBroader or hypothesisMapping. Please read the skos:scopeNote for the expected behaviours."""^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string> .
ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#broaderApplicative> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """All compositeNarrowerMappings will be applied to the context (i.e., the axioms resulting as the *outcome* of the broaderApplicative object mapping). This implies the following rules:\n\n- The broaderApplicative object must be a DataMapping or subclass thereof.\n- An exactRBoxMatch or inverseRBoxMatch MUST be provided to indicate the relationship between the subject (outcome of this mapping) and the object (on the other end of the relationship).\n\nSpecifically, this instruction means:\n\n- Consider the context/outcome axiom of this (subject) mapping, refer to it as the "child"\n- Look up the broaderApplicative mapping, refer to it as the "parent"\n- Find the axiom (or entry point into a digraph of axioms) created by the "parent" mapping, that is related to the "child" axiom along the relationship defined by the exactRBoxMatch\n- Apply the compositeNarrowerMappings of the subject (mapping) to the parent's axiom(s) and not to the child's\n\nFormally, this is modelled as Kleisli composition for a context monad (see Foundations §2.4). The co-occurrence constraint requiring an exactRBoxMatch is enforced by GCI Axiom 2.14a."""^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string> .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork#templateMapping> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#scopeNote> """When a partial mapping intended for use as a "template" is created, any compositeNarrowerMapping that is also a partial (rather than a complete) mapping, should be associated via compositeNarrowerTemplate.\n\nNB: where multiple composite narrower mappings exist on both the subject and object, the following semantics shall apply:\n\nIf the narrower mapping on the subject explicitly refers to a narrower mapping of the object, that assertion shall take precidence. \n\nIf the composite narrower mappings of both the subject and the object are modelled using skos:OrderedCollection, then the ordering of both collections will be respected. Should the size of the respective collections differ, the smaller of the two will be taken as the range of applicable mappings for the whole.\n\nIf the composite narrower mappings of either subject or object are members of the DataMapping class or subclasses thereof and, members (by inference) of the IndexedMapping class, then the mappingIndex shall be used to correlate the templates and non-templates together, whether via exact indexA == indexB semantics, or by linking the indexes to the ordering of an skos:OrderedCollection."""^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string> .

ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/creator> <https://github.com/nebularis> .
ontology/mork/spec/Mork.ttl only-in-tree <http://www.nebularis.org/ontologies/Mork> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/description> """MORK states a mapping between a source and a target ontology as data. A mapping is a node in a graph that says which source element corresponds to which target element, in which stratum of the target (its classes, its properties or its individuals), how closely, how confidently and under what governance. Mappings compose into a directed acyclic graph, so that the order in which they must run is derived and never written down.\n\nA compiler reads the mapping graph and writes executable artefacts, such as RML mappings, SPARQL queries, SHACL shapes and SWRL rules. A language model may propose the graph, and a validator and a person then check it before anything compiles. The module also holds Executable, the vocabulary for the plans, artefacts and diagnostics that MORK's Eligibility backends produce.""" .
